Services

Every blade, done right

From the knife block in your kitchen to the shovel in the shed — knives, blades, and garden tools. All brands welcome.

Knives & Blades

Straight & serrated

Kitchen & Chef Knives

Chef’s knives, santoku, paring, boning, and fillet knives restored to a clean, even edge — the workhorses of gumbo night, Sunday sauce, and everyday cooking.

Cutco & Double-D® Edge

Cutco’s recessed Double-D® edge takes the right touch to sharpen without ruining the pattern. It’s a specialty of the house — your Cutco set, handled the way Cutco owners hope for.

Specialty

Serrated Blades

Bread knives, steak knives, and serrated utility blades — yes, serrated can be sharpened. Each tooth is dressed so the blade bites and slices clean again instead of tearing.

Yes — serrated too

Pocket & Outdoor Knives

The folder in your pocket, the skinning and gut-hook knives at deer camp, the blade that cleans fish at the dock — pocket and outdoor knives sharpened to a working edge that holds up in the field.

Scissors & Shears

Kitchen shears, fabric scissors, and everyday scissors — blades dressed and the pivot set so they cut clean all the way to the tip instead of folding the material over.

Swords & Machetes

Long blades welcome. Swords and machetes get the room and the care they need — from a camp machete that clears the lease to a display piece you want kept right.

Garden Tools

Manual tools

Shovels

A sharp shovel bites into Louisiana soil instead of bouncing off it. Digging edges are cleaned up and re-beveled so the work goes faster.

Pruners

Bypass and anvil pruners sharpened and adjusted so they slice stems clean instead of crushing them — healthier cuts for the plant, easier work for you.

Hedge Trimmers

Manual hedge shears sharpened along both blades, so hedges and shrubs get trimmed clean instead of torn and chewed.

Axes

Axes and hatchets re-profiled and honed — a chopping or splitting edge that works with you through the woodpile, not against you.

Specialty Services

Repairs, edge work & classes

Repair — Nicks & Broken Tips

Broken tip from a drop on the tile? Nicks and chips from a bone or a frozen roast? Damaged blades are re-profiled and the tip rebuilt, then sharpened like the rest.

Nick & tip repair

Semi-Convex & Straight Edges

The edge geometry is matched to the work — a semi-convex edge for hard-use blades that take a beating, a crisp straight edge for kitchen and precision cutting.

Hand Sharpening on Request

Prefer your blade finished entirely by hand on the stones? Just ask — hand sharpening is available upon request for the knives that deserve the slow treatment.

Upon request

Sharpening & Honing Classes

Learn to keep your own edge. Jordan teaches sharpening and honing classes — stone work, holding an angle, and stropping — so your knives stay sharp between visits.

Classes

Certified Cutco Sales & Service — free sharpening and replacements forever

Jordan is a certified Cutco sales and service provider. Own Cutco? Your sharpening and replacements are covered — free, forever. Ask about the full Cutco line while he’s there, too.

About the Sharpener

Jordan McGee of Eunice, Louisiana

Jordan McGee — Owner / Professional Sharpener.

Cajun Knife Sharpening is Jordan McGee of Eunice, Louisiana — a craftsman who turned an obsession with a true edge into a mobile service for Acadiana. He’s listed as a knife sharpener with the Louisiana Custom Knife Association, in the company of the state’s custom makers and bladesmiths.

No storefront to drive to — Jordan brings the bench to your kitchen, camp, or business. One person, start to finish: the hands that answer your call are the hands on the stone.

  • Local & accountable — based right in Lafayette, not a mail-in warehouse.
  • Edges matched to the blade — a fillet knife, a chef’s knife, and a hunting blade don’t get the same treatment.
  • Specialty edges welcome — Cutco Double-D®, serrated, and damaged blades included.

Made for Louisiana Kitchens

Sharp knives are Cajun cooking equipment

Around here, a knife isn’t decoration. It cubes the meat and sausage that start the gumbo, breaks down the trinity, fillets redfish and specs at the cleaning table, and slices boudin and andouille. Cooking like this wears an edge down fast — and a dull knife makes every one of those jobs harder and more dangerous.

When those knives go dull, help is one call away — from somebody who cooks the same food you do.

Questions

Before you call

Do you sharpen serrated knives?+

Yes. Serrated blades — bread knives, steak knives, serrated utility and tomato knives — are sharpened tooth by tooth so they bite cleanly again instead of tearing.

Do you sharpen Cutco knives and the Double-D® edge?+

Yes — Cutco is a specialty. The Double-D® edge has recessed cutting edges with protected points, and sharpening it correctly takes a specific approach so the pattern isn’t ground away. Straight-edge Cutco blades are sharpened like any fine kitchen knife.

Do you really come to me?+

Yes — it’s a mobile service. Call or text, and Jordan will let you know when he’ll be in your area and set up a time. Sharpening is done on site, by appointment.

What brands do you sharpen?+

Just about all of them — Cutco, the big German and Japanese kitchen brands, American hunting and pocket knife brands, and plenty of no-name workhorses besides. If it has an edge, ask. The honest answer is almost always yes.

Can you fix a broken tip or a chipped blade?+

Yes. Tip and chip repair is part of the service: the blade is re-profiled, the tip rebuilt, and the edge re-established, then sharpened and finished like any other knife. Send a photo by text if you want a straight answer on a badly damaged blade before booking.

How do I book, and how does payment work?+

Call or text (337) 349-9776, say what you’ve got and where you are, and you’ll be added to the route for your area. You pay when the work is done — and your knives go straight back into the block, sharp.
